questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go on exchange to an English-speaking country and to a country where I knew there was a strong focus on a good academic and social study environment.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was very good support both at the University of Copenhagen and at Trinity College. My academic advisor at the University of Copenhagen has been extremely helpful and quick to respond to questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a full introduction week with many orientation sessions and social events at the university. We were assigned a tutor whom we could contact with questions. In addition, we were offered a buddy who was a student at Trinity College. My buddy gave me a tour and was always happy to answer any questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy for me to find a place to live. However, I started looking early, as the University of Copenhagen had warned us about a housing crisis. The housing crisis is real, and it makes accommodation expensive, and the living conditions were not particularly good.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: it is expensive and can be hard to find.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We received some information by email from Trinity College, and apart from that, the process was very straightforward. They have developed videos that you can follow, which makes the process very easy and accessible.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had made videos that we could watch, provided information on their website, and were easy to get in contact with.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wished/registered for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I found the process to be straightforward, but it is a good idea to have the university’s email contact information ready in case you need to get in touch with them if any issues arise.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of difficulty varied from course to course, and the exam format is quite different from what we are used to at the University of Copenhagen. Several of the courses did not have a final exam at all, but instead relied on assignments and tests throughout the semester, which together made up the final grade.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching consisted exclusively of lectures, with no seminar-based teaching. I missed having seminars, as I learn best when I am actively participating in the classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
European Human Rights
Food Law
Medical Law and Ethics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Food Law and Medical Law and Ethics were to really interesting courses.

questions.answer: nothing.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The housing was quite expensive. However, this was also because I paid for a longer period than I actually stayed. It is probably possible to find something cheaper or more flexible if you rent private accommodation.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Trinity College has a wide range of clubs and societies that you can join for 2–4 euros for the entire semester. I joined several clubs, all of which had a great sense of community.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I signed up for pottery classes, arts classes, fitness, the running club, and the hiking club. However, there are over 100 clubs available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The pottery-class was very fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went on several train trips to places including Galway and Belfast. They were really lovely cities, and the trips were very enjoyable. In addition, all the museums are free, which also made for some great experiences.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it very easy. I didn’t experience any culture shock and felt that I fit in well in the city and with the other students.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the clubs; it made it easy to find a community and meet other students. Also, sign up to have a buddy; that way you’re guaranteed to have a local friend from the start

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don’t think I experienced any cultural challenges.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature is really beautiful. I enjoy running a lot, and the city is great for that as well.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be open-minded, push some of your boundaries from home, and embrace all the experiences you can get. And most importantly, enjoy it—time flies, and it’s truly a special period in your life.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that the teaching is somewhat different, and I personally found this a bit challenging, as I was unsure whether I was studying “correctly.”

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from other cultures and learning a lot about myself.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living with people from other cultures. It was challenging to live with others who had very different habits regarding cleanliness, cooking, and so on. However, it might simply have been new to me, as I had never lived with anyone other than my partner or alone before.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It has been an amazing experience—look forward to it!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
